summary:
Walk left to right counting unclosed `(`. A `)` with nothing open needs one inserted `(`; whatever `(` remain
open at the end each need one inserted `)`. Those two kinds of leftover brackets can never fix each other, so
the sum is the minimum. O(n) time, O(1) space.

question.md:
Insert the fewest brackets anywhere to make `s` balanced. Return how many.

- **Insertions only:** nothing is deleted or moved.
- **Two kinds of problem:** a `)` that arrives with nothing open, and a `(` that never gets closed. `))((` has
  both: it needs 4 insertions.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Already balanced: insert nothing.
- Only `)`: each needs a `(` inserted before it.
- Only `(`: each needs a `)` inserted after it.

think.md:
**Why a stack.** In a well-formed bracket string, the bracket opened most recently must be closed first: brackets
nest, they never cross. "Most recent first" is exactly last-in, first-out, so keep the open brackets on a stack: push
on an opener, and on a closer check (and pop) the top. With a single kind of bracket the stack only ever holds `(`,
so a **counter** of open brackets can replace it.

**Which brackets can't be matched?** Scan left to right with a counter of open `(`. A `)` with nothing open is
stray: it needs one `(` inserted before it. Any `(` still open at the end needs one `)`. Each stray bracket needs
its own partner (one inserted bracket can't serve two of them), and the matched ones need nothing, so the answer
is the number of stray brackets. For `())(()((`:
Stray `)`: 1; still open at the end: 3. Total **4**.

approaches.title: Delete matched pairs until none remain

idea.md: Repeatedly delete `()` pairs; whatever remains can't be matched, and each leftover bracket needs one insertion.

lines.text: Cancel matched pairs, layer by layer, until none are adjacent.
Every leftover bracket needs one inserted partner.

steps.text: Left over: ')(((', 4 brackets, each needing one insertion.

walk.title: Repeatedly delete adjacent '()' pairs. Every bracket left over needs a partner inserted.

limits.md: Repeated deletions rescan the string; a counter finds the same leftovers in one pass.

approaches.title: One counter

idea.md:
`open` counts unmatched `(` so far; `added` counts `)` that arrived with nothing open. The answer is
`added + open`.

build: `(` → open + 1; `)` → close one if possible, else count an insertion.

lines.text: `)` with nothing open: insert a `(` before it.
Plus one `)` for every `(` still open at the end.

steps.text: ')' with nothing open: insert a '(' before it (added = 1).
3 '(' still open need ')' at the end: 1 + 3 = 4.

walk.title: Count currently open '(' as you go. A ')' with nothing open needs an inserted '('; '(' still open at the end need inserted ')'.

takeaways.md:
- **Minimum insertions to balance:** count stray `)` plus leftover `(`.
- One kind of bracket → a counter replaces the stack.
- **Pitfall:** letting the counter go negative instead of counting a stray `)`.
